pathlab.title: PathLab
pathlab.cardDescription: Visualizer for pathfinding algorithms on a weighted grid with BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, and A*.
pathlab.detailDescription:
PathLab

PathLab is an interactive visualizer for learning and comparing pathfinding algorithms. It uses a weighted grid with start and target points as well as fields such as wall, water, and mud.

The focus is understandable algorithm visualization: BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, and A* can be run individually or compared. The app separates path, cost, and runtime from the animation.

The project is a stable portfolio version with a GitHub Pages demo, automated tests, and a GitHub Actions workflow.
meta: Stack: React, Vite, JavaScript, CSS, Vitest
pathlab.learning: Keeping algorithms separate from React components, writing tests for edge cases, and making UI state understandable.

sortlab.title: SortLab
sortlab.cardDescription: Sorting algorithm visualizer with bar chart, controls, statistics, and explanation area.
sortlab.detailDescription:
SortLab

SortLab is an interactive visualizer for sorting algorithms. Users can see step by step how an array is sorted, adjust speed live, and compare different algorithms.

It includes Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, Quick Sort, and Heap Sort. The dashboard shows comparisons, swaps, steps, and runtime in milliseconds.

The project is a learning project for algorithms, React state, and visualization.
sortlab.learning: Connecting animation, speed control, and statistics so the algorithm stays visible and usable.

vsw.title: VSW - Vulnerability Scanner Web App
vsw.cardDescription: Defensive full-stack web app for low-risk security checks on authorized domains or IPs.
vsw.detailDescription:
VSW - Vulnerability Scanner Web App

VSW is a joint project with Botond. The app runs defensive, passive, or low-risk checks and displays results in a React dashboard.

The focus is on HTTP security headers, TLS/certificate information, a small safe port list, reports, and exports. The project contains a FastAPI backend, a React frontend, tests, and Docker basics.

Important: The project is explicitly intended for owned systems or systems with permission. It contains no exploits, no brute force, and no aggressive scans.
meta: Stack: FastAPI, React, TypeScript, SQLite/PostgreSQL, Docker
vsw.learning: Clearly limiting defensive checks, separating backend and frontend, and presenting results understandably.

besp2074.title: BESP2074
besp2074.cardDescription: Local Balkan economy simulation with Python model, JSON export, and web dashboard.
besp2074.detailDescription:
BESP2074

BESP2074 is a local, year-based Balkan simulation. The project uses a Python model, structured JSON data, and a local web dashboard to display scenarios up to 2074.

The app is intended as a learning and scenario simulation. The results are not real economic, political, or financial forecasts, but simplified model runs with assumptions, seeds, and optional events.

The project is usable locally but is not yet published as a finished public application.
besp2074.learning: Connecting model assumptions, JSON export, and dashboard so local scenarios remain understandable.

foliolint.title: FolioLint
foliolint.cardDescription: Local Python CLI for checking repositories for portfolio readiness, README structure, and public presentation quality.
foliolint.detailDescription:
FolioLint

FolioLint is a local, rule-based Python CLI for repository checks. The tool checks whether a project is documented well enough for a portfolio and whether key information such as README, status, setup, and public presentation quality is understandable.

The focus is on simple, explainable rules instead of black-box analysis. The project fits directly into my portfolio because it helps me clean up my own repositories systematically.
meta: Focus: repository quality, README checks, automation
foliolint.learning: Structure rule-based checks so they stay understandable and lead to real improvements in project repositories.
